edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ἀδελφοί μου, λίαν ἐκκέχυμαι ἀγαπῶν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑπεραγαλλόμενος ἀσφαλίζομαι ὑμᾶς: οὐκ ἐγὼ δέ, ἀλλ’ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, ἐν ᾧ δεδεμένος φοβοῦμαι μᾶλλον, ὡς ἔτι ὢν ἀναπάρτιστος: ἀλλ’ ἡ προσευχὴ ὑμῶν εἰς θεόν με ἀπαρτίσει, ἵνα ἐν ᾧ κλήρῳ ἠλεήθην ἐπιτύχω, προσφυγὼν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ ὡς σαρκὶ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ὡς πρεσβυτερίῳ ἐκκλησίας. [2] καὶ τοὺς προφήτας δὲ ἀγαπῶμεν, διὰ τὸ καὶ αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον κατηγγελκέναι καὶ εἰς αὐτὸν ἐλπίζειν καὶ αὐτὸν ἀναμένειν, ἐν ᾦ καὶ πιστεύσαντες ἐσώθησαν, ἐν ἑνότητι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ὄντες, ἀξιαγαπητοι καὶ ἀξιοθαύμαστοι ἅγιοι, ὑπὸ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μεμαρτυρημένοι καὶ συνηριθμημένοι ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τῆς κοινῆς ἐλπίδος.
pass_a_gloss: My brothers, I am exceedingly poured out in loving you, and rejoicing beyond measure I safeguard you; yet not I, but Jesus Christ, in whom I am bound and fear all the more, as being still incomplete. But your prayer to God will make me complete, so that I may attain the lot in which I have received mercy, having taken refuge in the gospel as in the flesh of Jesus, and in the apostles as in the presbytery of the church. And let us love the prophets too, because they also made their proclamation with the gospel in view, and hoped in him and waited for him; and believing in him they were saved, being in the unity of Jesus Christ, saints worthy of love and of wonder, attested by Jesus Christ and have been counted together in the gospel of our common hope.
pass_b_english: My brothers, I am poured out exceedingly in my love for you, and in overflowing joy I safeguard you. Not I, though, but Jesus Christ. Bound in him, I fear the more, as one still incomplete. But your prayer to God will complete me, so that I may attain the lot in which I was shown mercy, having fled for refuge to the gospel as to the flesh of Jesus, and to the apostles as to the church's presbytery.

And let us love the prophets as well, because they too made their proclamation with the gospel in view, hoped in him, and waited for him. Believing in him they were saved, standing in the unity of Jesus Christ: saints worthy of love and of wonder, attested by Jesus Christ, and numbered together in the gospel of our common hope.

choices.english: I am poured out exceedingly in my love for you
choices.why: Perfect passive of ἐκχέω with λίαν; keeps his self-spending image.
rejected: I am greatly enlarged in loving you

choices.english: not yet made complete / make me complete
choices.why: Same root twice; the martyr not yet finished. Paired English keeps the echo.

choices.term: προσφυγὼν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ ὡς σαρκὶ Ἰησοῦ
choices.english: having fled for refuge to the gospel as to the flesh of Jesus
choices.why: The gospel is his refuge as if it were Jesus' own flesh; ὡς kept.
ἐν ᾧ is 'in whom', not 'for whose sake'.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF 'for whose sake being bound' loosens ἐν ᾧ (in whom); ANF 'greatly enlarged' is weak for ἐκκέχυμαι (poured out); ANF supplies '[us]' after 'reckoned along with'.

notes: Source shows 'ᾦ' for ᾧ and 'ἀξιαγαπητοι' without accent; reproduced as supplied.

review.notes: Checked paragraph [1] in full. Ἀδελφοί μου, λίαν ἐκκέχυμαι ἀγαπῶν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑπεραγαλλόμενος ἀσφαλίζομαι ὑμᾶς matches A 'I am exceedingly poured out in loving you, and rejoicing beyond measure I safeguard you' and B 'I am poured out exceedingly in my love for you, and in overflowing joy I safeguard you'. Negation and agency of οὐκ ἐγὼ δέ, ἀλλ’ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός are kept ('yet not I, but Jesus Christ' / 'Not I, though, but Jesus Christ'). ἐν ᾧ δεδεμένος φοβοῦμαι μᾶλλον, ὡς ἔτι ὢν ἀναπάρτιστος matches 'in whom I am bound and fear all the more, as being still incomplete' and 'Bound in him, I fear the more, as one still incomplete'. Future ἀπαρτίσει and purpose ἵνα ἐν ᾧ κλήρῳ ἠλεήθην ἐπιτύχω, προσφυγὼν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ ὡς σαρκὶ Ἰησοῦ, καὶ τοῖς ἀποστόλοις ὡς πρεσβυτερίῳ ἐκκλησίας are preserved, including the ὡς comparisons. Hortatory καὶ τοὺς προφήτας δὲ ἀγαπῶμεν, the εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον / εἰς αὐτὸν infinitives, ἐν ᾧ πιστεύσαντες ἐσώθησαν, ἐν ἑνότητι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ὄντες, and ὑπὸ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ μεμαρτυρημένοι καὶ συνηριθμημένοι ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τῆς κοινῆς ἐλπίδος are present in both. Notes disclose OCR 'ᾦ' and unaccented 'ἀξιαγαπητοι'. No quoted scripture clause and no false citation. Title 'Refuge in the Gospel' names προσφυγὼν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ rather than a bare locus.

Source identity confirmed: Ignatius, Philadelphians 5, per Lake 1912 Loeb edition. Completeness: all clauses from the single Greek paragraph rendered in both Pass A and B; no omissions. Negation: 'οὐκ ἐγὼ δέ, ἀλλ’ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός' correctly rendered as 'Not I, though, but Jesus Christ' (Pass B) and 'yet not I, but Jesus Christ' (Pass A). Agency: subject-action relations preserved (e.g., 'your prayer to God will make/complete me'). Modality: indicative and future forms accurately reflected. Doctrine: Incarnational refuge ('gospel as the flesh of Jesus') and Christocentric unity maintained. Scripture: no explicit scriptural citations in source; apparatus-only references absent; thus no citation checks needed. Title 'Refuge in the Gospel' names the thought, not just locus. Notes disclose OCR-normalized forms (ᾦ for ᾧ, unaccented ἀξιαγαπητοι). No uncertainties. All checks pass.
